docs.title: Welcome to Canopy
docs.text:
Canopy is a community app store for umbrelOS with apps Umbrel's own store doesn't have, plus apps that other community stores ship years out of date. Every app is pinned to an exact release, checked for new versions every day, and installed and tested before an update reaches you.

It's also the home of YAMS, a complete media server (Jellyfin, Sonarr, Radarr, Prowlarr, Bazarr and qBittorrent behind a VPN) that comes already wired together.

Install Canopy Set up YAMS

The website always shows each app's current version and when it was last updated.

docs.title: Store rules
docs.text:
• Only apps that aren't in Umbrel's official store, or that other stores ship badly out of date.
  • Every image pinned to a release tag and its digest, from the app's official publisher.
  • Runs on amd64 and arm64.
  • Apps with their own login skip Umbrel's login (no double sign-in). Apps without one stay behind Umbrel's login.
  • Least privilege: nothing gets the Docker socket, host folders or capabilities it doesn't need. (Netdata reads container names through a read-only proxy that can't start, stop or change anything.)
  • No secrets in the repository. Passwords come from Umbrel (APP_PASSWORD, shown on the app's page) or are generated on the device.

docs.title: How Canopy stays current
docs.text:
Every morning a GitHub Action runs tools/ship_updates.py:

  1. Check. For every image it asks the registry for newer releases. Only real releases count: a tag must look like the one in use (v, number of parts, suffixes like -alpine), so betas, release candidates and nightlies are ignored. Databases stay on their major version; language runtimes on their minor version.
  2. Verify. A new version must run on both amd64 (Umbrel Home, PCs) and arm64 (Raspberry Pi), and must have been built after the one in use. Images are pinned by digest, and rebuilt tags (security fixes) refresh the digest.
  3. Test. tools/umbrel_sim.py installs the updated app exactly the way umbrelOS does (same folders, environment and container names, app_proxy replaced by a check) and confirms every container stays up and the web UI answers.
  4. Ship or ask. Patch, minor and rebuild updates that pass go straight to main, and Umbrel offers them within the hour. Major versions, and anything that fails, become a pull request with the test output attached.

Every pull request also runs the unit tests, the store rules (tests/test_store.py), the online checks (tools/lint_store.py: both CPU architectures, no port clashes with Umbrel's official store or other popular stores, no duplicates of official apps) and the install test for each changed app.

docs.title: Canopy (October 2026)
docs.text: The YAMS store became Canopy, a store for apps Umbrel doesn't have yet, kept on their latest versions. - 10 new apps: Netdata, JDownloader 2, openHAB, SiYuan (all badly out of date elsewhere), plus linkding, Miniflux, NZBGet, Feishin, ByteStash and Mylar3 (on no other Umbrel store). - Daily update bot: finds new releases, checks they run on amd64 and arm64, installs each one the way umbrelOS does, and ships it, or opens a pull request for major versions and failures. - Store checks on every pull request: store rules, pinned images, both CPU architectures, no port clashes with Umbrel's official store or popular community stores, no duplicates of official apps, and an install test for each changed app. - New website with every app's current version.

docs.title: YAMS 1.4.0
docs.text:
• Extras: Seerr, Lidarr, Recyclarr, Unpackerr and Decluttarr, each switched on from the dashboard and connected automatically. Off, they use almost no memory.
  • Fixed: Sonarr and Radarr refused to save qBittorrent while the VPN wasn't set up yet, so new installs could end up without a download client. It's now saved switched off and switched on as soon as qBittorrent runs.
  • Restoring a backup from the old yams-media app re-points Bazarr, Prowlarr's FlareSolverr and every other connection at the new containers.
  • First-run setup, the 10-minute checks and Quick fixes no longer race each other into duplicate entries.
  • App id is now canopy-yams (store id canopy). Back up, uninstall the old YAMS, install from Canopy and restore.

• Security hardening. The media apps moved to a private network other Umbrel apps can't reach. The dashboard's controls are only served to the router (behind your Umbrel login), and every command must come from the dashboard page, blocking cross-site requests. Security headers on every page.
  • Change password updates Jellyfin, qBittorrent, Sonarr and Radarr together. The password is hidden on the dashboard until you press Show.
  • A secret scan in the test suite fails the build if a password, VPN key or API key is ever committed.
  • Update apps yourself. The dashboard checks Docker Hub for newer versions and updates every app with one click, or automatically each week. It backs up your settings first and rolls back any app that won't start.
  • Quick fixes: connect Prowlarr or qBittorrent to Sonarr and Radarr, fix library folders, rescan Jellyfin, search for missing episodes and movies, reconnect the VPN, or fix everything at once.
  • Prowlarr is now linked to Radarr as well as Sonarr, using each app's own form, and the links are re-checked every 10 minutes.
  • GitHub Pages install guide, contributing guide, automated tests and CI.
• Sonarr and Radarr reliably get qBittorrent as their download client, re-checked and repaired every 10 minutes.
• Fixed qBittorrent failing to start ("unable to exec /app/qbittorrent-nox").
• Backups, like yams backup: on demand or automatic, with one-click restore.

• Logs, restart and VPN check for every app; update check; download list; home-screen widgets.
  • qBittorrent waits for the VPN tunnel itself rather than gluetun's health check.
• New app icon. qBittorrent is pulled from Docker Hub.
• First release.

docs.title: Contributing to Canopy
docs.text: Thanks for helping. Whether it's a new app, a bug report, a clearer sentence on the YAMS dashboard or a new feature, contributions are welcome. You don't need to be an expert: plenty of useful changes are a few lines.

docs.title: Ways to help
docs.text:
• Report a problem. Open an issue with the app, its version and its logs (YAMS: the dashboard's Logs button; other apps: right-click the app in Umbrel → Troubleshoot).
  • Add an app. See Add an app below.
  • Suggest an improvement. The best ideas start with "I keep having to…".
  • Improve the words. The dashboard is written for people who've never run a media server. If something confused you, it will confuse others.
  • Fix or build something. Look for issues labelled good first issue, or comment on one to say you're taking it.

docs.title: Add an app
docs.text:
Canopy carries apps that aren't in Umbrel's official store, or that other community stores ship badly out of date. Check the official store first.

  1. Make a folder named canopy-<app> (lowercase, dashes). Copy a similar app as a starting point: canopy-linkding is a single container with its own login, canopy-miniflux has a database, canopy-jdownloader uses the Downloads folder.
  2. docker-compose.yml. Pin the image to a release tag and its digest: image: publisher/app:1.2.3@sha256:…. python3 -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'tools'); import registry; print(registry.digest('publisher/app:1.2.3'), registry.architectures('publisher/app:1.2.3'))" prints both, and the architectures must include linux/amd64 and linux/arm64. app_proxy's APP_HOST is canopy-<app>_<service>_1. Keep data under ${APP_DATA_DIR}/data. If the app has its own login, add PROXY_AUTH_ADD: "false" so people don't sign in twice; if it needs a password, use ${APP_PASSWORD} and set deterministicPassword: true in the manifest so Umbrel shows it.
  3. umbrel-app.yml. id matches the folder, version matches the image tag (without a leading v), and pick a port no other app uses (the checks will tell you if one clashes). Quote the tagline. Write the description for someone who's never heard of the app.
  4. Test it like umbrelOS installs it: 
    python3 tools/umbrel_sim.py canopy-<app>            # install, check, remove
python3 tools/umbrel_sim.py canopy-<app> --keep     # leave it running to try it
python3 tools/umbrel_sim.py canopy-<app> --down
    It needs Docker and runs as root (it sets folder ownership the way umbrelOS does).
  5. Run the checks: pytest -q tests (offline rules) and python3 tools/lint_store.py canopy-<app> (architectures, ports, duplicates), then python3 tools/build_site.py to add it to the website.
  6. Open a pull request. CI runs all of the above again, including the install test. Once merged, the update bot keeps the app current from then on.

docs.title: How the project fits together
docs.text:
umbrel-app-store.yml          store id "canopy"
canopy-<app>/                 one folder per app
canopy-yams/
  umbrel-app.yml              the App Store listing, version and home-screen widgets
  docker-compose.yml          every container, including the Extras
  hooks/yams/                 all of YAMS's own code (see "Rules" for why it lives here)
    setup/seed.py             first boot: keys, passwords, starter configs, folders
    dashboard/server.py       dashboard API, app wiring, quick fixes, widgets, Docker controls
    dashboard/extras.py       Extras: switches, their settings files, Seerr's setup
    dashboard/updater.py      "Update apps": registry checks, image pulls, container recreation
    dashboard/backups.py      backup, restore and the backup schedule
    dashboard/index.html      the dashboard page
    extras/gate.sh            keeps an Extra waiting until it's switched on
    vpn/vpn-wrapper.sh        starts gluetun once a VPN file exists
    qbittorrent/*.sh          the VPN kill switch for qBittorrent
    Caddyfile                 routes each app's web UI behind the Umbrel login
tools/                        install simulator, update bot, store checks, website builder
docs/                         the GitHub Pages site
tests/                        automated tests (run on every pull request)

docs.title: Run the tests
docs.text:
You need Python 3.12 or newer.

pip install pytest pyyaml
pytest -q tests

The tests use fake versions of Docker, Sonarr, Radarr and Prowlarr, so they run anywhere in about twenty seconds, with no Umbrel needed. They also check every app against the store rules and that the website lists every app. Every pull request runs them automatically, plus the install test for each app it changes.

docs.title: Try your change on your own Umbrel
docs.text:
1. Fork this repository on GitHub and push your change to your fork.
  2. Raise the app's version in its umbrel-app.yml (for YAMS, for example 1.4.0 → 1.4.1-test, and set YAMS_VERSION in docker-compose.yml to the same value).
  3. In Umbrel, go to App Store → ⋯ → Community App Stores. Remove this store and add your fork's URL instead. Both use the store id canopy, so only one can be added at a time.
  4. YAMS shows an Update button (or install it fresh). The dashboard header shows your test version once it's running.
  5. When you're done, switch back to https://github.com/Deepshah0308/canopy-umbrel-store.

Umbrel re-copies hooks/yams/ on every update, so code changes reach your Umbrel whenever you bump the version.

docs.title: Rules that keep YAMS safe and working
docs.text:
• Keep code in hooks/yams/. umbrelOS only re-copies certain files when an app updates, and the hooks folder is one of them. Code elsewhere would reach new installs but never existing ones. Never name a file after a hook (pre-start, post-update, …) because umbrelOS would run it.
  • Standard library only. The dashboard runs on the stock python:alpine image, so there's nothing to pip install. This keeps installs fast and nothing to build.
  • qBittorrent only ever uses the VPN. It shares gluetun's network, waits for the tunnel before starting, and stops if the tunnel goes. Any change near this needs a test showing downloads can't leave outside the VPN.
  • Only touch YAMS's own containers. Anything using the Docker socket filters by the com.docker.compose.project=canopy-yams label.
  • Check what an app accepted. When wiring apps together, start from the app's own schema (…/schema endpoints), then confirm the change worked before marking a step done. Otherwise failures go silent.
  • Write for newcomers. Messages say what happened and what to do next, in plain words. "Can't reach qBittorrent right now. YAMS checks again every 10 minutes." beats "Connection refused (111)".
  • Add a test for any behaviour you change. The fakes in tests/fakes.py make most things easy to test.

docs.title: Releasing a version
docs.text:
App updates are shipped by the daily update bot (see the README). Major versions arrive as pull requests: read the app's release notes for breaking changes, then merge.

For YAMS itself, maintainers release by merging to main with the version bumped in both canopy-yams/umbrel-app.yml and YAMS_VERSION in canopy-yams/docker-compose.yml (a test checks they match), plus a line in CHANGELOG.md. Umbrel then offers the update to everyone.

docs.title: Be kind
docs.text: Treat everyone with respect. Assume good intent, explain rather than dismiss, and remember many people here are running a server for the first time. Harassment or personal attacks aren't welcome and will be removed. If something bothers you, open an issue or contact the maintainer.

docs.title: License
docs.text: Canopy is MIT licensed (see LICENSE), and contributions are shared under the same license. Each app keeps its own upstream license.

docs.title: Frequently asked questions
docs.text:
How do I add a community app store to Umbrel?

In Umbrel, open the App Store, click ⋯ in the top right and choose Community App Stores. Paste https://github.com/Deepshah0308/canopy-umbrel-store and click Add. Canopy's apps then show up in their own section of the App Store.

How do I install Jellyfin, Sonarr and Radarr on Umbrel together?

Install YAMS from Canopy. It sets up Jellyfin, Sonarr, Radarr, Prowlarr, Bazarr and qBittorrent behind a VPN in one install, already connected to each other, with a dashboard to finish setup. See the YAMS overview.

Do I need to use a terminal?

No. Add the store address, click Install. Apps that need a login show it on their page in the App Store.

Is it safe?

Community stores aren't reviewed by Umbrel, so it's fair to ask. Every app is pinned to an exact, published version from its official publisher, apps without their own login sit behind your Umbrel login, and nothing gets more access than it needs. See Security, and report problems privately.

Will it work on my Raspberry Pi?

Yes. Every app must run on both Umbrel Home and PCs (amd64) and on Raspberry Pi (arm64), and the store's checks refuse any version that doesn't.

Can Jellyfin use my graphics card?

Yes, on umbrelOS 2.1 or newer. See Hardware transcoding.

Umbrel's terminal says a YAMS container is not running

Update YAMS to 1.4.5 or newer. Older versions opened Umbrel's terminal in the one-time setup container, which always stops after it finishes.

An app I want isn't here.

Suggest it. If Umbrel's official store already has it, install it from there; Canopy doesn't duplicate official apps.

Something's broken.

For YAMS, try Quick fixes → Fix everything on its dashboard first, then see Troubleshooting. Otherwise open an issue with the app's logs (right-click the app in Umbrel → Troubleshoot).

docs.title: Install Canopy
docs.text:
No terminal needed. You only add the store once; after that, Canopy's apps show up in Umbrel's App Store next to the official ones.

  1. In Umbrel, open the App Store, click ⋯ (top right) and choose Community App Stores.
  2. Paste this address and click Add:

https://github.com/Deepshah0308/canopy-umbrel-store
3. Open Canopy and install whatever you like. Umbrel warns that community apps aren't reviewed by Umbrel; that's expected.

docs.title: Updates
docs.text: Canopy checks every app for new releases each morning, tests them, and ships them. Umbrel then shows an Update button on the app, the same as for official apps.

docs.title: Removing Canopy
docs.text: Uninstall any Canopy apps you no longer want, then in App Store → ⋯ → Community App Stores remove Canopy's address.

docs.title: Reporting a problem
docs.text:
Please don't open a public issue for security problems. Use GitHub's private reporting instead: go to the repository's Security tab and choose Report a vulnerability. You'll get a reply within a few days, and a fix will be released as a new version of the affected app.

A problem in an app itself (say, a bug in Miniflux) belongs with that app's authors; Canopy ships their fix as soon as they release it.

docs.title: How every Canopy app is packaged
docs.text:
• Exact, verified images. Every image is pinned to a release tag and its digest, so what you install is byte-for-byte what was tested. Images come from each app's official publisher.
  • Updates are tested before they ship. The daily update bot installs each new version the way umbrelOS does and only ships it if it starts and answers. Major versions wait for a person.
  • Least privilege. No app gets the Docker socket, host folders or extra capabilities unless it needs them. Netdata, which needs to see your containers, gets a read-only proxy that can list them but can't start, stop, change or run anything in them.
  • Logins. Apps with their own login skip Umbrel's login so you don't sign in twice; apps without one stay behind your Umbrel login. Generated passwords come from Umbrel and are shown on the app's page.

docs.title: How YAMS on Umbrel protects you
docs.text:
• Downloads only use the VPN. qBittorrent runs inside the VPN container's network, starts only when the VPN tunnel is up, and stops within seconds if it drops. gluetun's firewall blocks everything else.
  • Other Umbrel apps can't reach YAMS's apps. Sonarr, Radarr, Prowlarr, Bazarr, qBittorrent, Jellyfin and the VPN live on a private network of their own. Only the router joins Umbrel's shared network, so every web page sits behind your Umbrel login.
  • The dashboard's controls aren't on any network. They're served on a file socket that only the router can reach. On the network, the dashboard answers only the two read-only home-screen widgets.
  • Commands must come from the dashboard page. Each one carries a custom header that other websites can't add, so a malicious page open in your browser can't send commands.
  • Secrets stay on your Umbrel. Passwords, API keys and the VPN key are generated on first boot and stored in files only root can read. The dashboard hides the password until you press Show. Change password updates Jellyfin, qBittorrent, Sonarr and Radarr together.
  • Docker access is limited. The dashboard uses Docker only for YAMS's own containers, identified by their Compose project label.
  • Extras keep secrets private. Settings files for Recyclarr, Unpackerr and Decluttarr contain API keys and are readable only by their owner. Decluttarr never removes private-tracker torrents or torrents you added yourself.
  • Backups contain secrets. They include the password, API keys and VPN key so a restore works. They're saved in Downloads → yams-backups with owner-only permissions. Keep downloaded copies somewhere private. If you share your Downloads folder on your network, anyone with access to that share can read them.

docs.title: For contributors
docs.text: Never commit real passwords, API keys or VPN files, including in tests or examples. Use obvious placeholders like not-a-real-password. The test suite scans the repository for YAMS-style passwords, WireGuard private keys and API keys, and fails if it finds one.

docs.title: YAMS
docs.text:
YAMS (Yet Another Media Server) packaged so a complete beginner can go from "install" to "watching" without a terminal or a config file. Open it after installing and the dashboard walks you through four steps: connect a VPN (paste a WireGuard file), add indexers in Prowlarr, add a show or movie, and watch in Jellyfin at http://umbrel.local:8097.

Moving from the old YAMS store (yams-umbrel-store, app id yams-media)? The old and new YAMS use the same ports, so they can't run side by side. Backups are kept in your Downloads folder, which uninstalling doesn't touch:

  1. In the old YAMS, open Backups and press Back up now.
  2. Uninstall the old YAMS (your media and backups in Downloads stay).
  3. In Community App Stores, remove the old YAMS store and add Canopy's address.
  4. Install YAMS from Canopy, open Backups and restore the backup from step 1.

Settings, logins, VPN and library come across, and YAMS re-points every connection to its new containers. Jellyfin keeps port 8097, so TV and phone apps keep working.

Next steps

See what YAMS sets up for you, switch on Extras, and learn the dashboard.

docs.title: What YAMS sets up for you
docs.text:
Normally you'd have to… YAMS on Umbrel does it for you Run Jellyfin's setup wizard and create libraries Creates the admin user and Movies + Shows libraries, with real-time folder watching Copy API keys between apps Generates keys up front and wires Sonarr, Radarr, Prowlarr and Bazarr together Add qBittorrent to Sonarr and Radarr Done, with tv / movies categories Set library folders /data/media/tv and /data/media/movies, hardlink-friendly (TRaSH layout) Set up FlareSolverr Added to Prowlarr with the flaresolverr tag Write gluetun environment variables Paste a WireGuard file; the hostname is resolved to an IP and IPv6 is stripped, which gluetun requires Turn on file renaming On in both Sonarr and Radarr Log in to five different web UIs Everything except Jellyfin sits behind your Umbrel login

The one thing left for you inside an app is picking subtitle languages in Bazarr → Settings → Languages.

docs.title: Extras
docs.text:
Optional apps that ship with YAMS, off until you switch them on in the dashboard's Extras section. While off, each one only runs a tiny wait loop. When you switch one on, YAMS writes its settings and connects it:

Extra What YAMS sets up for you Seerr (port 7475) Signs in to Jellyfin, turns on the Movies and Shows libraries, adds Sonarr and Radarr, finishes the setup wizard. Family members sign in with their Jellyfin accounts. Lidarr Music root folder, qBittorrent (category music), Prowlarr link, and a Music library in Jellyfin Recyclarr Syncs the TRaSH Guides quality sizes plus a WEB-1080p profile (Sonarr) and HD Bluray + WEB profile (Radarr), daily; Seerr then requests with them Unpackerr Watches Sonarr, Radarr (and Lidarr) for .rar downloads and unpacks them Decluttarr Removes stalled, failed and slow downloads and searches again. Never touches private-tracker torrents or torrents you added yourself

docs.title: How it fits together
docs.text:
Umbrel login ──► web (Caddy) ─┬─ /            dashboard (setup + auto-wiring)
                              ├─ /sonarr      Sonarr
                              ├─ /radarr      Radarr
                              ├─ /prowlarr    Prowlarr ── FlareSolverr
                              ├─ /bazarr      Bazarr
                              └─ /qbittorrent qBittorrent ─┐
                                                           │ shares network with
port 8097 ──► Jellyfin                          gluetun (WireGuard VPN)

Downloads can't leak. qBittorrent runs inside gluetun's network, so its only route out is the VPN, and gluetun's firewall blocks everything else. On top of that, qBittorrent won't start until the VPN tunnel (tun0) exists, and a watchdog stops it within about 10 seconds if the tunnel disappears. When you switch VPN files, YAMS stops qBittorrent first, reconnects, then brings it back.

Files live in Umbrel's Downloads folder: Downloads/torrents (in progress) and Downloads/media (your library). Because both are on one mount, Sonarr and Radarr hardlink finished downloads instead of copying them, so seeding doesn't double your disk usage.

docs.title: Managing YAMS
docs.text:
Once setup is done, the YAMS dashboard becomes the control panel for the whole stack (the equivalent of the yams command-line tool):

YAMS CLI On Umbrel yams check-vpn VPN check compares your home address with the one downloads use, and confirms qBittorrent is inside the VPN yams logs Logs on every app, live-updating, with errors highlighted and a Copy button yams restart Restart on every app, or Restart all (the VPN is restarted before qBittorrent so it reconnects cleanly) yams backup Backups: back up on demand or automatically (daily or weekly, keeping the last 3, 5 or 10), and Restore any backup with one click yams update Update apps checks Docker Hub and updates every app to its newest version with one click, or automatically each week. It backs up your settings first

Two widgets are available for the Umbrel home screen: a stats card (VPN, downloads, shows, movies) and a live list of active downloads. Right-click the home screen and choose Edit widgets to add them.

Backups work like yams backup: apps pause for a moment so their databases are saved cleanly, then every app's settings and history, your logins and API keys, and your VPN file go into one .tar.gz in Downloads → yams-backups. Caches, logs and cover art are left out (they rebuild themselves), and your media files are never included. Automatic backups run between 3 and 5 AM, Umbrel's clock.

Restoring checks the file first: it must be a YAMS for Umbrel backup that contains nothing but app settings, or it's refused before anything stops. YAMS then saves a safety backup of your current setup, swaps the restored settings in and starts the apps. If anything fails part-way, the previous settings are put back. You can restore on a fresh install too: install YAMS, upload your backup (or copy it into Downloads → yams-backups with the Files app) and choose Restore.

Backups contain your passwords and VPN key, so keep copies somewhere private.

Quick fixes repair the most common problems with one click: connect Prowlarr to Sonarr and Radarr, connect qBittorrent to them, fix library folders, rescan Jellyfin, search for missing episodes and movies, and reconnect the VPN. Fix everything runs the first three. Each fix checks first and only changes what's wrong. YAMS also re-checks the Prowlarr and qBittorrent connections every 10 minutes by itself.

Search through the VPN. If your internet provider blocks indexer sites, switch on Search through the VPN under VPN check. Prowlarr's searches and FlareSolverr then go out through the VPN too, the same idea as YAMS's Prowlarr behind VPN guide but with no compose editing. They use the VPN container's built-in proxy rather than its network, so Prowlarr still reaches Sonarr and Radarr directly. If the VPN drops, searches pause instead of going around it.

Two kinds of updates. App updates (new Sonarr, Jellyfin and so on) happen from the YAMS dashboard whenever you like. The apps use moving tags such as latest, so YAMS can check Docker Hub, download new images and swap each container for a new one with identical settings. It backs up your settings first and rolls back any app that won't start. YAMS updates (new dashboard features and fixes) arrive through Umbrel's own Update button when a new version is published here.

Security. The media apps sit on a private network other Umbrel apps can't reach, and every web page is behind your Umbrel login. The dashboard's controls are only reachable through the router, never the network. Your password is hidden until you press Show, and Change password updates every app at once. See SECURITY.md for details and how to report a problem privately.

Docker access. The dashboard mounts the Docker socket so it can read logs, restart containers and update apps, the same approach Umbrel's Portainer and Dozzle apps use. It only ever acts on containers that belong to the YAMS app (by their Docker Compose project label), and can't restart itself.

docs.title: Hardware transcoding
docs.text:
Jellyfin can use your Umbrel's graphics card to convert video on the fly, which is much faster and quieter than using the CPU.

Needs umbrelOS 2.1 or newer and YAMS 1.4.6 or newer

YAMS asks Umbrel for GPU access, and Umbrel passes in whatever graphics hardware it finds (Intel, AMD or NVIDIA). It's re-applied on every update, so you never edit a compose file. Older umbrelOS versions ignore the request.

docs.title: Turn it on in Jellyfin
docs.text:
Jellyfin has two menus called "Playback". The transcoding settings are in the admin Dashboard, not your user settings.

  1. Open http://umbrel.local:8097/web/#/dashboard/playback/transcoding, or click ☰ → Dashboard, then ☰ → Playback → Transcoding. You need the admin login shown in the YAMS dashboard under Your login.
  2. Set Hardware acceleration:
    • NVIDIA NVENC for NVIDIA cards
    • Intel QuickSync (QSV) or Video Acceleration API (VAAPI) for Intel and AMD graphics
  3. Tick the codecs your card supports under Enable hardware decoding for, then Save at the bottom.

docs.title: Check it works
docs.text:
Play something and force a lower quality in the player. In Dashboard → Activity, the stream should say it's being transcoded with your hardware. If playback fails, switch Hardware acceleration back to None, save, and open an issue with Jellyfin's transcode log.

See Jellyfin's own guides for NVIDIA and Intel.

docs.title: Troubleshooting YAMS
docs.text:
Start with Quick fixes → Fix everything in the YAMS dashboard. It solves most connection problems.

  • qBittorrent says "Waiting for the VPN". Open Logs on the VPN row. The last lines say why the tunnel isn't up (an expired key, an unreachable server). Downloading a fresh WireGuard file for another server fixes most cases.
  • An app says "Keeps restarting". Its row shows the last log line; open Logs for the full story.
  • VPN says "Can't connect". Download a file for a different server. Some providers' files expire, and a few (e.g. NordVPN) don't offer WireGuard downloads at all; Proton VPN, Mullvad and AirVPN all do.
  • Port 8097 is taken. Denny's store has an Emby app on the same port; you can't run both. Otherwise change 8097:8096 in docker-compose.yml and JELLYFIN_PORT on the dashboard service to the same new number.
  • You changed the qBittorrent password. Update it in Sonarr and Radarr under Settings → Download Clients.
  • Logs. Use Logs on any app in the YAMS dashboard. Umbrel's own Troubleshoot view (right-click YAMS) works too. Lines starting with [yams] come from this package.
  • Start over. Back up first, then uninstall YAMS (this deletes its settings, not your media or backups in Downloads) and install again. Restore the backup if you want your settings back.
  • A restore went wrong. Every restore first saves a "Before restore" backup; restore that one to get back to where you were.

docs.title: Known limits
docs.text:
• VPN setup supports WireGuard files. OpenVPN-only providers aren't covered by the dashboard yet.
  • VPN port forwarding isn't configured, so torrents work but may connect to fewer peers.
  • Hardware transcoding needs umbrelOS 2.1 or newer, which passes your graphics card (Intel, AMD or NVIDIA) to YAMS. Then pick it in Jellyfin under Dashboard → Playback → Transcoding (VAAPI or QSV for Intel/AMD, NVENC for NVIDIA).
  • Only the Downloads folder is used; external drives need Umbrel 2.0's folder access feature or a manual mount.
